title: Introduce presubmit cost sampler and toolchain stabilizer
author: Priya Natarajan
release_notes: Adds a low-volume presubmit cost sampler and a toolchain stabilizer that reduces CI variance (no user-facing API changes). Backfill: recommended for teams experiencing noisy CI due to toolchain churn.
description: Context: CI noise from transitive dep updates and toolchain version flips has led to intermittent presubmit failures and unpredictable cost spikes in hosted runs. Motivation: reduce noise, gather sample-based cost telemetry, and stabilize the dev toolchain so presubmit failures are actionable rather than transient. What this PR does: 1) Adds a lightweight presubmit-cost-sampler pipeline (ci/presubmit/sampler.yaml) that runs on ~0.5% of PRs and records job-level time/cpu/mem/infra-cost estimates to the internal CI-telemetry store. 2) Introduces a toolchain-stabilizer service (infra/toolchain-stabilizer/) that: - pins a curated minimal set of tool versions for presubmit lanes, - warms language/OS-specific caches on ephemeral runners, - injects a cache-warm header into existing install steps. 3) Adds an opt-in "quiet-merge-window" gating policy (scripts/merge-window/README.md) that batches non-urgent merges during off-peak windows to reduce peak CI contention. 4) Adds a small metrics exporter (tools/ci-metrics/exporter.go) and a docs page (docs/ci/cost-sampler.md) describing cost metrics and how teams interpret them. Backwards compatibility: all changes are opt-in via two repo-level feature flags (repo settings): ci.cost_sampler and ci.toolchain_stabilizer. Default rollout: ci.cost_sampler=false, ci.toolchain_stabilizer=false. Rollout plan: stage 1 (internal): enable both flags for redwood/* small teams (1 week) and validate stability. Stage 2 (canary): enable ci.toolchain_stabilizer=true for 10% of active repos and ci.cost_sampler=true at 0.5% PR sample rate (2 weeks). Stage 3 (gradual): increase sampler to 2% and stabilizer to 50% if metrics are green. Testing done: - Unit tests for exporter and stabilizer boot sequence - End-to-end smoke against ephemeral runners (ci/presubmit/smoke) - Canary presubmit runs recorded in telemetry (see CI checks) Checklist: - [x] Feature flags implemented - [x] Minimal docs added - [x] Telemetry schema versioned (v1) - [x] Quick rollback path (feature flag off) Known limitations: sampler estimates are model-based and may over/under-estimate infra cost by ~10% initially; we will calibrate over next 2 weeks. Related: ENG-1456 (presubmit-costing), ENG-1489 (toolchain hygiene).
